episodes.215414: A backdoor front pushed through eastern New Mexico during the morning hours of August 19th resulting in an uptick in thunderstorm activity across the higher terrain and nearby lower elevations of central New Mexico. Thunderstorms producing locally heavy rainfall resulted in debris flow in and below the 2024 South Fork burn scar. Severe thunderstorms also produced large hail along the eastern slopes of the Sangre de Cristo Mountains and severe wind gust in the Sevilleta National Wildlife Refuge.
episodes.215478: During the late night/early morning hours of August 18th/19th, 2026, a storm brought large hail and widespread damaging wind gusts across Leavenworth County and Wyandotte County, KS. A NWS Storm Survey showed a swath of 60 to 80 mph winds across Kansas City, KS, with widespread tree and power line/pole damage. Power was out area-wide for up to a week, with some areas not seeing power restored for several weeks.
episodes.215501: On the 19th afternoon to overnight, the active mid-August pattern brought another round of thunderstorms and locally heavy rain across central Indiana.  Despite only near-normal warmth and dewpoints, a train of multiple upper short wave troughs flowing west to east over the Midwest, around a deep 500 mb low near James Bay, promoted training downpours and occasional rotating cells.  Main activity trended from multiple rounds of numerous cells over far northern zones through afternoon and early evening hours, down through the Interstate 70 corridor later in the evening, to an early overnight resurgence of strong/severe cells from west-central to southeastern central Indiana.||Flash flooding was the primary impact, in areas where an additional 3.00-4.50 inches of rain fell;  in the evening from the Lafayette area to Madison County, and later in the overnight in mainly Putnam County.  Overall isolated damaging winds were focused in the evening from Tipton to Delaware County and briefly during the overnight in Putnam County.  Large hail, up to 1.50 inches, and a very brief EF-U tornado were both confined to a cell crossing Delaware County around 1630 EST.
episodes.215806: Scattered thunderstorm activity associated with weak shortwaves passing through the Tennessee Valley region resulted in several reports of wind damage over the span of two afternoons and evenings.
episodes.216225: A weak area of low pressure rode along a stalled frontal boundary across the coast of eastern North Carolina gradually pushing offshore during the overnight hours of August eighteenth to the morning of August nineteenth. Along and out ahead of this front, isolated showers and thunderstorms developed with a few of these storms becoming severe in nature as they tracked east across the Pamlico Sound and out into the coastal waters of Eastern North Carolina. The strongest storms brought strong wind gusts with them to portions of the Pamlico Sound.
episodes.216361: A thunderstorm produced a 64 mph wind gust at the ASOS (Colorado Plains Airport) located near Akron.
episodes.216418: Showers and scattered thunderstorms produced several funnel clouds during the late afternoon and early evening of August 19th.
episodes.216574: Multiple rounds of showers and thunderstorms produced several wind gusts in excess of 34 knots.
episodes.216702: Scattered supercells developed over north central Kansas during the evening and overnight hours on the 18th.  Hail up to golfball size in diameter and wind gusts to 70 mph were reported with these storms.
episodes.216801: Typical summer weather prevailed with scattered afternoon and evening storms, some of which were severe. In addition, an area of slow moving thunderstorms produced flash flooding in and near Dothan.
episodes.216944: A near severe thunderstorm developed during the afternoon hours of August 19th over northwestern Puerto Rico. This thunderstorm produced small hail, strong wind gusts, and torrential rainfall that led to urban and small stream flooding.
episodes.216945: A waterspout developed over the coastal waters of Naguabo in southeastern Puerto Rico on August 19th.
episodes.217008: Typical summer weather prevailed with scattered afternoon and evening storms, some of which were severe.
episodes.217012: Typical summer weather prevailed with scattered afternoon and evening storms, some of which were severe.
episodes.217481: A warm and humid air mass supported afternoon thunderstorms August 19th. A brief landspout tornado occurred in southwest Louisa County Iowa the afternoon.  No damage was found along the path of the weak, intermittent tornado, which was seen by many people.
episodes.217528: Afternoon thunderstorms reached severe levels in Navajo County, producing large hail in some areas.
episodes.217536: A warm and humid air mass supported afternoon thunderstorms August 19th. Isolated strong storms brought gusty winds and a report of a funnel cloud the afternoon of August 19th, 2026.
episodes.217588: A shortwave trough initiated elevated thunderstorms over central Nebraska during the morning of August 19th. With time, upscale growth of these thunderstorms into an organized thunderstorm complex occurred. A surface based bowing line segment would mature over eastern Nebraska producing damaging wind gusts up to 70 mph and large hail up to 1 inch in diameter.
episodes.217591: During the early afternoon of August 19th, a lingering surface boundary and rapidly developing thunderstorms interacted, producing several pronounced funnel clouds in far western Iowa. A remnant outflow boundary helped to initiate several weak thunderstorms in western Iowa during the evening of October 19th. These thunderstorms produced several instances of pronounced and highly-visible funnel clouds. No touchdowns or damage was reported with any of these reports.
episodes.217594: Thunderstorms developed during the afternoon along a slow moving boundary over central Ohio. Some of the storms produced locally heavy rainfall.
episodes.217679: Ahead of a warm front, showers and storms began to propagate southeast. Though most storms were able to stay below severe limits, a few thunderstorms were able to dip into around 1000 J/kg of DCAPE and weak shear over northeast Mississippi producing damaging wind gusts. Thunderstorms continued south of the Mid-South through sunset as instability began to wane.
episodes.217696: A cold front crossing the area, combined with increasingly warm and moist air during the afternoon, resulted in the development of some storms during the evening on the 18th, which produced some wind damage and a few instances of small hail.
episodes.217699: A cold front crossing the area, combined with increasingly warm and moist air during the afternoon, resulted in the development of some storms during the evening on the 18th, which produced some strong winds and small hail.
episodes.217823: On August 18th, weak shortwave energy moved through the eastern periphery of the Heat Wave ridge over a moist and unstable airmass enhancing storms mainly over northeast and central Florida. Scattered showers and storms developed along the inland-moving sea breezes with stronger storms, capable of wet microbursts, pulsing along mesoscale boundary collisions in the afternoon into evening. On August 19-20, a frontal boundary stalled over southern Georgia as ���Heat Wave��� ridging built in from the west. Tropical moisture of 2+ inches of precipitable water remained south of the front, mainly over northeast Florida. Scattered showers and storms developed along the inland-moving sea breezes. The combination of high moisture, strong diurnal heating, and sea breeze/outflow interactions supported strong to severe storms capable of producing damaging winds, frequent lightning strikes and torrential downpours. Weak steering flow allowed for localized flooding. On August 22nd, lingering upper shortwaves ahead of the weakening frontal boundary in central Georgia triggered morning showers and isolated storms moving inland from the Gulf. Convection then spread east-northeastward through the day in the general southwest flow. A few stronger storms occurred along sea breeze boundary mergers in the late morning to early afternoon hours in north-central Florida.
episodes.217922: A thunderstorm developed along a backdoor cold frontal boundary across southwest Minnesota during the early evening of August 18. Shear and instability parameters were sufficient to produce marginally large hail.
episodes.217929: During the early morning hours of August 19th, storms brought damaging wind gusts and large hail to portions of western Missouri, primarily Jackson County.
episodes.218050: A surface boundary spawned a cluster of thunderstorms, which produced hail up to ping pong ball size in Western Kansas. The storms were moving southeast in the afternoon and early evening hours.
episodes.218117: Large-scale ridging aloft and coastal troughing at the surface in combination with a moderately unstable airmass supported thunderstorms capable of damaging winds.
episodes.218164: A cold front moving across the warm waters of Lake Erie during the morning hours of August 19 caused a broken line of showers and thunderstorms to develop. A number of waterspouts were reported from near the Cleveland area and points northeast on Lake Erie with these showers and thunderstorms.
episodes.218266: The Black Hills saw two days of marginal severe weather, that brought wind and hail to the Black Hills and surrounding areas.
episodes.218530: Isolated thunderstorm development occurred along a boundary intersection across central Kansas that resulted in a severe wind and hail report.
episodes.218559: An upper low over the state coupled with deep tropical moisture created unstable environment favorable for convection that produced a strong marine wind gust over Tampa Bay.
episodes.218560: An upper low over the state coupled with deep tropical moisture created an unstable environment favorable for convection that produced thunderstorm wind damage near Wildwood in Sumter County.
